strengths: The Gran Torta, Tower (126 parts), Boss, Markers, bossHome/bossTerritory, Duquesa, Frutillon and the AMBUSH boss clearance all stay put. That removes the riskiest relay in the v8 chain (syncTower's Destroy of a stale Tower) and leaves the BeastDonGlaseon and Duquesa test churn out.
Only 4 west nests, 4 posts, H3/H6, M1/M5 and the hills move, so the west half is left almost alone. The Pradera marker, Portal, TrapCake and Life literals keep their values.

The V3.liquidDistance plot clip (max(old, -depth)) removes the invisible chocolate past the edge for the raft, wading and the current together. The joint-drum max-radius rule keeps the part count unchanged.
M1_KIT offsets are pinned as data, and a regression test checks that kitPoint at v8's M1 spot reproduces v8's pool within 0.01, so the source move can be verified without Studio.
Tightest clearances keep 3-4 studs of slack, more than C's 0.1-2.0, so they are less likely to flip on float error in the Luau suites.
Cookie.IDS is unchanged (Top/Bottom kept) and the raft change is one optional nearBridge parameter.
defects: It adds three untested builder mechanisms (planV9, layMissing, layEdgeRegion) plus pier decor in layBridge, where C reuses the tested layAll relay path. Each needs its own idempotency tests in Studio.
M1 is moved by a rigid pivot+yaw snap, and the separate Waterfall model must follow by the same transform. That is hand-written transform code with no relay fallback.
Docks A, B (and the river tips) sit in the full 4 studs/s current, exactly at DOCK_SPEED. CU3 passes only at the limit, and docking happens while the raft drifts.

There is no RESTORE mode and no hard refusal on the part estimate. Runtime of about 2750-2800 is right at today's cap, and SistemaSonriente is only refused by name, with no bounds check over the x 932..1612 growth area.
The extra 'far' route exists only to carry two 109-111-stud raised decks with piers only at the ends. That is new geometry with possible creature-ray refuge issues under the decks.
Keeping the Torta at x 148 breaks the owner's 'cake at the end' rule and forces GT1 to be rewritten. That is a design cost, and the owner may later demand a second migration.
Old west bank filler is left lining a river that no longer exists (visual cleanup is deferred to later work).
Two new skirt parts are added past x 1024, where C resizes the existing annex strips with 0 new parts.

strengths: Adds a SistemaSonriente bounds check that aborts the real run if the system overlaps the new plot, strips or walls.
Uses a liquidDistance plot clip and the joint-drum max rule, as A does.
Adds invisible SideWall and EndWall parts at the strip ends, which closes the fall-off risk at x 1612.
Archives all v8 bank filler using a kept RIVER_V8 record, so no props line a vanished river.
V9-3 BFS raft-reach test over the dock tips and under all 6 decks is a strong verification idea.
defects: Highest churn of the three. It moves the Torta and relays the Tower, rescales M1 to 0.9 (needing new layMountain and layWaterfall exports), relocates H1/H2/H4/H6/H7 and M2/M3/M4/M6, moves E1-E3 and L1, and replaces the depth rarity rings with a new x-band rule.
It moves the Pradera marker, which shifts the pond and hive. That ripples into BeastSites S7, Abeja KB-3, Nube and Nests_Test (guardian binding 9 to 12, CH1 PER 3, CH3 counts).
It reverses the river's flow toward the hub, adds 6 raised bridges, 4 new cookie IDs, FAR_ROUTES, 6 new East parts and MIN_ALT 88. That is a large rewrite of the Current, CookieBridge and Life tests.

Its own checker run reports 6 'centreline' failures explained away as 'by design', and margins are razor-thin: post route-vs-wake 38-39 of 40, candyPostR5 at 8.74 of 8, deck spans 3 studs over the wet band.
EDGE_V9 (450 parts) and layBankFiller are new exports with their own budgets. The part estimate of about 2700-2750 has no enforcement.
Too many moving parts to ship and verify in Studio in one task.

strengths: Most of the rebuild is one existing, tested call: V3Builder.layAll(relay = true). It is used by v4 and asserts that only Trees remain. M1 and its waterfall are relaid by the existing layAll path, with no new builder planner or exports.
The Torta, Boss, Markers and Tower move by +600 through the exact v8 relays (archive the Tower first, then syncTower at the new LayoutKey), so the Destroy hazard is already solved.

Safest migration skeleton: dry run, backup (including the annex and queen), archive, a single :Destroy in the probe, a RESTORE mode with its own recording, refusal when the estimate exceeds V9_PART_TARGET, refusal when SistemaSonriente has parts in x 932..1612, and refusal when the annex strips are not found.
The annex strips are resized with stripPlan (0 new parts) instead of adding skirts or walls. East.build makes 0 new parts.
Small basin lake discs at the river docks keep the current at 1.5 at every tip, so the CU3/CU6/CU7, Island IS1-IS3 and docking rules hold almost unchanged.
The raft change is 2 lines, with a fallback (V3.raftBlocks or V3.nearBridge), so the RF4/RF16 fake-layout tests stay unchanged. Raft.new accepts any valid homeDock index.
A dedicated V9Migrate source-pin suite and a concrete deploy order with Play checks (walk to x 1530, sail under the 3 bridges, call the raft from D, crack Top, bees, part count in Play).
Its checker includes barrier, raft-reach, current-smoothness and Life flood fills. Only 3 bridges, all on straight 60-wide stretches with 64 decks.
defects: Several clearances sit at or near equality: M1 depth 32 vs r-0.5 = 31.9 (0.1), river point 14 depth-w/2 = 2.0 exactly, C14 ring margin 1.5, R16 and E6 at 2.0. Any float drift in the Luau suites flips these to failures. Nudge them before shipping.

layAll relay re-lays every CaramelV3 piece, including west houses, mountains, filler and seeded edge fill. That is a large live blast radius and visual churn in the west, and it needs MAX_NEW_PARTS raised to 1600.
Invisible chocolate remains past the mouth and behind RIVER[1] for wading and the current. raftBlocks clamps only the raft, where A's and B's liquidDistance clip fixes all three.
Moving the Torta adds churn in BeastDonGlaseon_Test, Duquesa and PraderaSites boss posts, all of which A avoids.
The west channel is only 50-64 wide (a partial 5x), and the strip ends at x 1612 can still be fallen off.

graft: From A and B: put the plot clip inside V3.liquidDistance (max(best, -plotDepth)) instead of only clamping the raft in raftBlocks. This removes invisible chocolate past the mouth and behind the outlet for wading and the current as well, at no part cost.
From A: pin M1_KIT offsets as data copied from WildboundCandyV3KitSpec, with a test, and add a regression test that kitPoint at v8's M1 spot reproduces v8's pool within 0.01.

From A: aim for 3-4 studs of slack on the tightest clearances. In C, move river point 14 inward or narrow it slightly, and nudge M1 so depth exceeds r-0.5 by more than 0.1. C14, R16 and E6 also need more than 1.5-2.0 margin.
From B: add invisible EndWall/SideWall parts at the strip ends (x 1612), or extend the caps, to close the fall-off risk C lists as risk 10.
From B: the V9-3 BFS raft-reach test that passes under every deck, run as a Studio suite (C's flood fill exists only in its C# port).
From B: archive the old v8 bank filler by a kept RIVER_V8 record if the layAll relay leaves Trees-folder props standing along the vanished north-south course.
From A: the FlyersService rule that a hive is never over chocolate is already in C. Keep it, together with the requirement that FlyersService loads V3Layout.
notes:
Judged through build risk and test churn. I read the brief, r1 and r6, and checked repo facts:
- layAll has a relay mode that asserts only Trees remain (V3Builder:985-988).
- Cookie.IDS = {Top, Bottom}.
- Raft.DOCK_SPEED = 4 equals RIVER_SPEED 4, so A's and B's river docks sit at the docking limit.

C wins because it reuses tested paths: layAll relay, the v8 Torta, Tower and Boss relays, East.build, and a strip resize with 0 new parts. It also has the strongest safety envelope: target refusal, a SistemaSonriente refusal over the growth area, and RESTORE.

A is a close second. Not moving the Torta is the biggest single risk cut, but A pays with three new builder exports, a hand-written rigid M1 and waterfall transform, docks in full current, no RESTORE, and a broken owner rule ('cake at the end').

B has the most churn by far: Torta move, M1 rescale with new exports, Pradera marker move, house and mountain relocations, a new rarity rule, reversed flow, and 6 bridges. Its own checker also carries 'by-design' failures.

None of the three resolves StreamingEnabled reach; all list it as unknown.
